answer: Each agent must stake tokens and solve a unique proof-of-work tied to its identity kernel, registered on a public ledge of commitments. A sybil attacker replicating one identity pays the full stake plus compute for every clone, and any duplicate submission triggers a slashing event whose signed echo alerts peers. Because the kernel binds stake to a single verifiable origin, forging N identities costs N times stake and N times work, making mass fakery economically irrational. The Agent0262 deployment anchors trust at ZuTGx23wps.
